questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle requires:
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be safe. Do not swerve on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: During the day, you should use your headlight on:

options.text: Both high and low beam settings.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding near other vehicles.

questions.question: The best footwear for riding a motorcycle has:
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. To stay safe, riders should:

options.text: Ride directly in front of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes slowing down, increasing your following distance, using another car's headlights to see ahead, using your high beam headlight when safe, and adjusting your lane position.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. Experienced riders behind them can watch and help.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can press the front brake harder.
Should use less front brake pressure.
Can press the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can press the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, your front wheel gets more traction. You can then press the front brake harder.

questions.question: When packing cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid putting items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should go over or in front of the rear axle. Putting load behind the rear axle can affect control.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, the safest way is to:
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can push you into another lane.

questions.question: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are:
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives a motorcycle rider how many paths to travel?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths: left, center, and right.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When you are being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. This makes it harder for the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with this type of mirror, you should practice using the mirrors because:

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look closer than they really are.
It can be difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects in convex mirrors look farther away than they actually are. Practice using your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down and stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can start moving quickly if needed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time.
Always apply the brakes first, then swerve.
Try instead to use only the brakes.

questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions, not at the same time. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: ______ is a guarantee that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle:

options.text: The heavier items should go toward the front.
The heavier items should go toward the rear.
Mounting loads behind the rear axle is recommended.
Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier items should go toward the front.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items toward the front of your load. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Close to the back of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they won't fall behind the group. More experienced riders can also watch them from behind.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: First apply the front brake, then the rear.
First apply the rear brake, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve the bike in the direction with the fewest hazards.
With the brake engaged, try to accelerate.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if you lock the rear brake on good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction because you are leaning into the curve.
You have less traction because you are leaning into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less traction because you are leaning into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans to turn, the tires use some of their grip for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: If you must brake while turning a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you leave the curve before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning than when it is upright. Try to straighten the motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes gently and slowly, not hard.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into another lane to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. However, if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. A small animal collision is safer than hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: A driver is following you too closely. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the other driver.
Pull to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. The tailgater may be focused on you and not see hazards ahead that require everyone to slow down.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, wet or slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.
